end.summary: Practised sums of consecutive odd numbers beginning with 1 and linked them to square numbers.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised using square grids and adding the new dots in an L-shape to explain why consecutive odd numbers make squares. They correctly found 25, 36, and 144 in examples, and explained that the added dots can be counted as 5 below, 5 to the side, and 1 corner dot. They still mixed up the rule by treating any run of odd numbers as a square, and this was not corrected by the end. At home, use small dot grids to build 1, then add 3, 5, 7, and ask Saanvi to show the new L-shaped dots each time.
